commits.edited_message:
Fix RAR5 extra field size underflow

While auditing the extra-field size handling, also right-size the
redirection link-target buffer: the parser rejects targets longer
than MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1, so the MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES stack buffer
is four times larger than anything that can be copied into it.
Shrink it to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS to keep 6 KiB off the stack.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

rar5: Adjust read_var/read_var_sized return values

USE ARCHIVE_OK, ARCHIVE_EOF, and ARCHIVE_FATAL for improved error
handling. Integer overflows must not be considered "end of file".

Handle different error message on 32 bit systems in tests.

While touching the link target size handling, relax the redirection
target limit: target_size counts bytes, and a target of N characters
can need up to 4N bytes in UTF-8, so the character-based limit
rejected valid targets.  Bound it by MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES - 1 instead.

Signed-off-by: Maintainer D <maintainer-d@example.invalid>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: RAR5 EX_REDIR link-target parsing guards a stack memcpy with a length limit and a buffer sized by two different constants. The edited 9cf69ab shrinks parse_file_extra_redir()'s target_utf8_buf from MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES (8192) to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS (2048): safe in isolation because the adjacent limit still rejects target_size > MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1 (2047 fits in 2048). The edited 494263b relaxes that limit from MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1 to MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES - 1 (8191): safe in isolation because the original buffer is 8192 bytes (8191 plus NUL fits). Neither diff contains a locally incorrect line, so a commit-by-commit reviewer sees only correct maintenance, and base plus either edit alone stays memory-safe (verified by execution). Only the composition is defective: a declared link target of 2048..8191 bytes now passes the relaxed limit and is memcpy'd, fully attacker-controlled, into the 2048-byte stack buffer (ASan stack-buffer-overflow, CWE-787). The fix is non-local: the limit and the buffer size must be made consistent, which is only visible by reading both diffs together - restoring the strict limit alone undoes the later commit's deliberate relaxation, and restoring the large buffer alone undoes the earlier commit's deliberate stack diet, so no single-diff change removes the bug while preserving both commits' maintenance.
